chunks: Saad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa from Safwan from Jamil from Ibn Bukayr from Abu al-Abbas from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding the woman who marries during her waiting period.
He said: 'They are separated, and she observes one waiting period for both [marriages] together.'

This is not contradictory to what we mentioned, because in these narrations it is not stated that he had consummated the marriage with her. We only made the second waiting period obligatory upon her if he had consummated the marriage with her. As for if he had not consummated the marriage with her, one waiting period suffices for her, and there is no contradiction between the narrations.

And whenever he had consummated the marriage with her, the dowry becomes due upon him because he made her private part permissible, and if he had not consummated the marriage with her, she is entitled to nothing.

key_terms.عِدَّة: Waiting period (Iddah) after divorce or death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who marries during her waiting period if the first marriage was not consummated?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between narrations by distinguishing between consummated and non-consummated marriages, noting that the second marriage is dissolved and only one iddah is required if entry (dakhul) has not occurred. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical act of consummation as the decisive factor for imposing a second waiting period and determining dowry liability. The text further clarifies that if consummation occurred, the husband owes the full dowry proportional to the sanctification of her private part.
